clue.text: Bird in pile of hay?

definitions.meaning: a male fowl, the rooster of the farmyard
a conical heap of hay stacked in a field, as in haycock

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the farmyard male fowl and a small stack of hay left to dry in a meadow.

clue.text: I manage, before end of dinner, to sink into deep sleep — many will laugh at that

indicators.note: to sink into means these pieces go down inside the other

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconsciousness
to cope is to manage

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word dinner

explanation.surface: Someone says they manage to fall into a deep sleep at the end of dinner, which will amuse many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sink into' puts I, COPE and R (end of 'dinner') inside COMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, humorous stage work set to music is meant to amuse an audience.

clue.text: Censors of wicked man who tells all?

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters behaving badly and falling into disorder

explanation.surface: Censors of a wicked man who blabbed everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' shuffles the letters of CENSORS OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes a full confession admits everything, as in Edward the Confessor.

clue.text: The traditional bedtime story?

parts.note: read not as a tale told at bedtime but as the storey of a house you climb to when going to bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' puns on 'storey', a level of a building; bedrooms traditionally lie upstairs, one level above the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrooms in a traditional house sit on the level just above the ground, so that storey is where bedtime happens.

clue.text: Fair son in trouble -as you'd expect after this word's been given

definitions.text: as you'd expect after this word's been given
definitions.note: the phrase describes a word that is normally followed by the word as

indicators.note: in trouble means these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A good-looking son is in trouble, just as you'd expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' shuffles the letters of FAIR SON. The definition is a riddle: the answer is the word usually followed by 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction is almost always used in the set phrase completed by 'as', meaning to the extent that.

clue.text: Cut off from highly respected new leader

indicators.note: new leader means the first letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: revered means highly respected

explanation.surface: Someone is cut off from a highly respected new chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new leader' replaces the first letter of REVERED, giving it an S in front instead of an R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chopped clean away has been cut off, as in a severed rope.

clue.text: The last thing colleagues expect to hear from one retiring

definitions.text: The last thing colleagues expect to hear from one retiring

parts.words: The last thing colleagues expect to hear from one retiring
parts.note: reads as something unexpected, but means the final address given by a departing colleague

explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing ... expect' looks like 'least likely', but the 'last thing' is the final words at a leaving party.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring employee traditionally gives a goodbye address as the final act of their working life.

clue.text: Willow looking healthier when pollarded

indicators.note: pollarding a tree cuts off its top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: rosier means pinker-cheeked, looking healthier

explanation.surface: A willow tree looks in better shape after being cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when pollarded' removes the top letter, R, from ROSIER. Pollarding, lopping a tree's crown, is often done to willows.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Film executive creating a row

definitions.meaning: J. Arthur ..., the British film magnate behind the ... Organisation

explanation.walkthrough: J. Arthur Rank was a British film producer whose company used the famous gong-man logo; a taxi rank is where cabs queue in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a famous British film mogul is also a word for a line, as of taxis or soldiers.

clue.text: With head down?

parts.note: read as having the soft fluffy plumage of birds stuffed inside one's skull

explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction, but it means soft feathers: a head filled with them is empty of sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone silly or scatty is said to have only fluff in their skull instead of brains.

clue.text: Pit for storing cold meat

indicators.note: a pit used for storing something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cold store for keeping meat chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced beef or lamb is chopped meat, sold as a staple at the butcher's.

clue.text: Even igor's possibly more than a prince

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A character named Igor is apparently of even higher rank than royalty's younger sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the nine letters of EVEN IGORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch outranks a prince, so a king or queen is literally more than a prince.

clue.text: Shed with few carrots thrown into storage unit

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Gardening scene: a shed and a handful of carrots get chucked into a storage space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' shuffles the fourteen letters of SHED and FEW CARROTS; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom cabinet fitted with sliding compartments is a piece of furniture for keeping clothes.

clue.text: Cap — something worn on head in China

parts.note: to cap is to crown, top off
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A cap is something people in China wear on their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is porcelain, not the country: the capital C hides it at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English maker of fine porcelain tableware.

clue.text: Former old city with housing for English chemist

indicators.note: the two pieces together provide housing for the next one, holding it inside

parts.note: former means past, bygone
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A description of an ancient city that once had lodgings for a visitor from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with housing for' puts E between PAST and UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French scientist who discovered pasteurisation, a celebrated chemist and microbiologist.

clue.text: Free a couple of notes getting stuck on the organ

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes of the scale
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A musician finds a pair of notes jammed on a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'organ' is not the musical instrument the notes suggest, but a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from danger is to rescue or set them loose, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Very bad, bringing in substitute that's deficient and variable

indicators.note: bringing in means the first word takes the other inside it

parts.note: vile means very bad

indicators.note: that's deficient means the word lacks something, here its final letter

parts.note: ersatz means substitute, artificial

explanation.surface: Something is very poor, using a weak replacement, and changeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's deficient' cuts the Z off ERSATZ, leaving ERSAT; 'bringing in' places that inside VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable that can change easily to suit many uses is flexible.

clue.text: Welsh food that seems to be a delicacy?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a ..., a choice morsel

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a Welsh dish sounds like something special.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into RARE BIT, a rare morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheese-on-toast dish's name, split into two words, describes an uncommon tasty morsel.

clue.text: Gut feeling that's denied in teaching

indicators.note: that's denied means the following word is refused, taken out of the first

parts.note: intuition is a gut feeling
taken as written, the word in

explanation.surface: A teacher's gut instinct gets overruled in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's denied' removes IN from the start of INTUITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruction given by a tutor, especially paid lessons, is schooling.

clue.text: Cover of Webster damaged

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the name are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: The cover of a Webster's dictionary has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' shuffles the letters of WEBSTER; 'of' only joins the definition to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew things all over a surface is to scatter them so they cover it.

clue.text: Short business letter sounding odd

indicators.note: sounding means the pieces are spoken aloud to give the word

parts.note: biz is a shortened form of business, as in showbiz; R is a letter, said as 'ar'

explanation.surface: A brief business letter comes across as strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, BIZ followed by the letter R ('ar') gives the word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird or peculiar strikes people as strange.

clue.text: Gal flirted with zeal — extraordinary female entertainer

indicators.note: extraordinary signals the letters being put into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: A girl flirted keenly, an extraordinary woman performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' shuffles the letters of GAL FLIRTED and ZEAL; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The American jazz singer known as the First Lady of Song was a celebrated woman performer.

clue.text: Where golfers play a wild cat may be heard

indicators.note: may be heard means the word is said out loud

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: On a golf course you might hear a wild cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Links are seaside golf courses, the original Scottish kind; the wild cat said out loud sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside golf course on sandy coastal ground is called by this name.

clue.text: A great worry when there's no end of trouble in the distance

indicators.note: when there's no means something is missing from the word for worry

parts.note: fear is a great worry

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: A big worry that stops once trouble is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's no' takes E, the end of 'trouble', out of FEAR, leaving FAR after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far away is a long way off, distant.

clue.text: Connoisseur going round home is an expert on money matters

indicators.note: going round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a fancier is a connoisseur or keen enthusiast, as in pigeon fancier
in means at home

explanation.surface: A connoisseur doing the rounds at home turns out to be good with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts IN (at home) inside FANCIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker or investor dealing in large sums is a specialist in finance.

clue.text: Noisy person in town starts to create racket, irritating every resident

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A loud townsman starts making a racket that annoys everyone living there.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the town crier, who called out public announcements in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who shouted news and proclamations through the streets.

clue.text: Dire scenes when these homes break up

indicators.note: break up means the letters are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Grim domestic scenes happen when households split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break up' shuffles the letters of DIRE SCENES.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses or flats where people live are their dwellings.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink in company

definitions.meaning: informal British word for a drink, often spelt bevvy
a group, as in a ... of beauties

explanation.definitionFit: One word is British slang for a boozy drink and also a collective noun for a group of people.
